title: Vana: exile
hook: Vyasa walks into the forest camp with a plan: the waiting can become preparation, and Arjuna must go alone
carry: let the waiting become a plan

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vana, the forest, where Bhima wanted to fight now, and Yudhishthira held to the word he gave. Your line was keep the word you gave.

An old sage walks into a stuck camp. Bhima wants them stronger, and soon. Yudhishthira won't break his word, and he knows how formidable the warriors on the other side are. The brothers are caught between impatience and patience. The visitor is Vyasa, grandfather of both the Pandavas and the Kauravas, and he has come with a way out.
screen: `STUCK BETWEEN IMPATIENCE AND PATIENCE.` → `VYASA WALKS IN.` → `WAITING BECOMES A PLAN.`

segments.voice: Vyasa takes Yudhishthira aside. I know what's in your heart, he says: the fear of Bhishma and Drona and Karna. So here's what to do. He gives Yudhishthira a sacred knowledge to teach to Arjuna, an inner discipline that will let him reach the gods. Arjuna must go, he says. He must seek out the gods themselves, Indra and Rudra and the guardians of the world, and win their weapons through ascetic effort. That is how the Pandavas will be ready when the time of exile ends. Now the argument looks different. Bhima wanted action, and here it is. Yudhishthira wanted to keep his word, and he does. Nobody breaks the terms; nobody leaves the forest early. But the waiting stops being empty. It becomes a time to grow. And notice the cost. Arjuna has to go alone. The brothers who have shared everything, even exile, will be apart. Yudhishthira teaches him what Vyasa taught, and Arjuna sets out, armed, toward the mountains of the north. In the epic, Draupadi speaks a blessing over him as he goes, wishing him success and asking the gods to protect him on the road. The forest has carried the Pandavas through a lot: the sun's vessel, Krishna's visit, the long arguments. Now it becomes a base camp. One brother walks out of it, and tomorrow we follow him up the mountain.
screen: `VYASA TAKES YUDHISHTHIRA ASIDE.` · `A KNOWLEDGE FOR ARJUNA.` · `SEEK THE WEAPONS OF THE GODS.` · then, large: `THE WAITING BECOMES GROWING.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind some waiting in your own life, a season you can't hurry or an answer that hasn't come, and feel how it sits in you as you breathe. On each breath out, ask gently what this waiting could be for, and let the question rest there without forcing an answer. If you pray, bring that waiting into your prayer; if not, rest in the question.
Vana. The forest of exile, which becomes a base camp the day Vyasa sends Arjuna to seek the weapons of the gods.
Your line: let the waiting become a plan. Vyasa didn't shorten the exile; he gave it a purpose. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Retellings of the Mahabharata mark Vyasa's visit as the turn in the forest years, when Arjuna leaves to seek divine weapons; tradition names Vyasa as the epic's composer as well as a character in it.

chat.says: What did Vyasa actually do for the Pandavas stuck in the forest?
options: He sent Arjuna to win the gods' weapons, so the waiting became a time to prepare.
He freed them from their promise, so they could go home before the years were up.
He told Bhima to stop complaining, since the exile was a punishment they deserved.
chat.meaning: Vyasa kept the terms intact but gave the exile a purpose: Arjuna would seek the gods' weapons, so the Pandavas would be ready when it ended.

Vyasa.meaning: the sage who is grandfather of both families

Kauravas.meaning: the Pandavas' cousins, the other side of the family

Rudra.meaning: a fierce god, a name of Shiva

Arjuna.meaning: the third Pandava brother, a great archer

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), Vyasa's visit to the Pandavas (the knowledge given to Yudhishthira for Arjuna; Arjuna sent to obtain weapons from the gods; Arjuna's departure and Draupadi's blessing)

notes: All paraphrase. Ganguli calls the knowledge 'Pratismriti'; the script describes it rather than naming it. Keeper may want the name.
